The album remains closed in its shallow box when you ask, “Could one of its photographs be displayed for the reopening?”

“Not under the agreement we have,” Nell says. “Public display is specifically excluded. So are scanning and publication.”

She taps the relevant clause without reopening the album.

“If there’s a particular photograph that later seems useful, record its written description and its position in the album. Don’t make a reference copy or take it downstairs to show people. Bring the catalogue reference to me.”

Any request would then have to identify the exact photograph, the proposed use and how long it would be displayed. Bea would need to approve those terms in a further written agreement.

“She’s already told me she wants to speak to the people pictured before deciding,” Nell says. “Some photographs were taken at family gatherings away from the cinema. She hasn’t begun those conversations, and we’re not going to turn the reopening deadline into pressure on her.”

Nell closes the permissions folder.

“Rosa hasn’t requested anything from the album, and her exhibition isn’t waiting for it. For now, the answer is no display.”

The album stays in the locked cupboard. Nell brings the transfer file back between you and resumes the first catalogue entry.
